To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 1D, 2D and 3D models of the human head phantom show that the magnitudes of the amplitudes of the transmission coefficients between the antennas of the future MWI system decrease from 0.9, to 0.5 and to 0.1, respectively.

the magnitudes of the amplitudes of the transmission coefficients of a MWI system with the 1D, 2D and 3D human head phantom models are in the range from 0 to 0.5, from 0 to -0.1 and from 0 to – 0.05 respectively.
the 1D human head phantom is not realistic enough to represent the human head in terms of electrical properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical simulations of the propagation of EM waves in the human head.
the development of a new generation of a microwave imaging system for stroke detection.
the numerical study of the propagation of electromagnetic waves in a human head phantom.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transmission coefficients between antennas are very low, which means that the MWI system is very sensitive to the electrical properties of a human head.
the 2D model of the head phantom represents the best compromise between the accuracy of the simulations and the required computational power.
the 1D human head model is the most realistic one and the 2D model is the worst one, which is a result of the simplifications in the 2D case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnitudes of the amplitudes of the transmission coefficient are very small, which means that the MWI system is not suitable for detection/classification of the stroke in the future.

the transmission coefficients of the 1D head model are the highest and the 3D model the lowest, which is expected due to the fact that the 1D and 3D models represent the highest and the lowest theoretical limit of transmission coefficient magnitudes, respectively.
the transmission coefficient between two antennas is a very sensitive function of the distance between the two antennas, the electrical properties of tissues and the shape of the head.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnitudes of the amplitudes of the transmission coefficients between the antennas of the MWI systems are not as high as one would expect.
the 1D numerical simulations are not sufficient for the design of the switching matrix.
it is possible to achieve the transmission coefficient magnities in the range of -40 dB to -60 dB for a 1D human head model, which is in agreement with the results from the literature.
